requirement.evidence: (a) It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord. (b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
requirement.note: Definition of algorithmic device (nonpublic competitor data of two or more landlords) and remedies (injunction, damages, penalties up to $1,000, fees to prevailing party) are also in the document. The card says fees for a winning tenant; the document gives fees to a prevailing landlord or tenant, a minor omission.

key_value.evidence: A tenant may seek injunctive relief, damages, or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation of this Division, in a civil action against a landlord.
key_value.note: Each month and each property as a separate violation is stated in §98.1103: "For each month a violation of section 98.1103(b) exists or continues, and for each residential rental property a landlord uses an algorithmic device, it shall constitute a separate and distinct violation."
